question.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-3,4,7)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $r\cdot ⟨-3,1,1⟩=9.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a point on the plane. If $r=⟨x,y,z⟩,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-3,1,1⟩ & =9 \\ -3x+y+z & =9 \\ z & =9+3x-y.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $x=1$ and $y=1,$ we get 

$$
z=9+3(1)-(1)=11.
$$

So, the point $Q(1,1,11)$ lies on the plane. 

Now, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,1,11⟩-⟨-3,4,7⟩ \\  & =⟨4,-3,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨-3,1,1⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|4\cdot (-3)+(-3)\cdot 1+4\cdot 1|}{\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-12-3+4|}{\sqrt{9+1+1}} \\  & =\frac{|-11|}{\sqrt{11}} \\  & =\frac{11}{\sqrt{11}} \\  & =\sqrt{11}.\end{aligned}
$$
